transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because… I don’t know how else to say it, but I keep hearing people talking about me. Like through the conference room walls, or sometimes from my phone even when it’s off, and it’s not vague. It sounds clear. It sounds like board members, staff—people I know—saying I’m ruining the company, that I’m not fit to be there, things like that.

And I know how that sounds, I do, but in the moment it feels completely real. I’ll actually answer them, like out loud, before I catch myself and realize nobody else in the room heard anything. Then I look around and people are staring at me, or they’re confused, and I feel… humiliated, honestly. It’s been happening enough that I can’t just brush it off anymore, and it’s affecting me at work.
How long has this been happening?

It’s been… about three months, I think. The voices from the walls, or sometimes from my phone, started happening around then. At first I tried to explain it away, like maybe I was overhearing something or maybe the phone had glitched somehow, but it’s kept happening over these last few months. It hasn’t just been one odd day. It’s been going on long enough that I can’t pretend it’s nothing anymore.
During these past three months, have you had a period where you felt unusually high, energized, or euphoric for days at a time?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, I guess. I mean, my job can be intense, and there are days where I’m running on adrenaline and coffee and trying to act like everything is fine, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt unusually euphoric or like I was on top of the world for days.

If anything, I’ve felt keyed up because I’m trying to keep myself together and not look unstable in front of people. But “high” or energized in a good way… no, I haven’t really noticed that.
During these past three months, have you had a period of feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed most of the day nearly every day. I mean, I’ve definitely been upset and worn down by all of this, and there are days where I feel embarrassed or scared or just exhausted from trying to function normally. But “depressed” feels like… I don’t know, maybe a specific thing, and I’m not sure that’s what’s been happening.

I haven’t really been tracking my mood that way. Some days I’m anxious and tense, some days I’m angry at myself for not being able to handle things better, and some days I sort of just push through because there isn’t really another option. But I can’t honestly say I’ve noticed a stretch where I’m depressed all day, almost every day. At least not that I can clearly identify.
Before these voices started, were you diagnosed with any medical or neurological illness?

Not that I know of. I mean, I’ve had the normal sort of things people have over the years, checkups and headaches here and there, getting run down from work, that kind of thing, but I was never told I had some neurological condition or serious medical illness before this started.

Unless you mean something very specific that I wouldn’t think to count? But no, there wasn’t some diagnosis beforehand that I can point to and say, “Oh, that explains it.”
Have you felt sure that people are deliberately trying to harm you or plot against you?

I don’t know if I’d say I feel sure of that. “Deliberately trying to harm me” sounds very… definite, and I don’t want to exaggerate or say something that makes it sound worse than it is.

I do get worried about people’s intentions sometimes, especially in situations where I’m already stressed, and I can replay things people said and wonder what they really meant by it. But an actual plot against me, like people organizing to hurt me… I can’t say I’ve felt certain of that. I haven’t noticed something that clear-cut.
Since these experiences began, has your ability to do your work dropped noticeably?

Yes. I mean… noticeably is almost an understatement, honestly. I’ve always been the person people came to when something needed a decision, or when things were messy and someone had to make a call. That was my job, really. But since all this began, I’m not reliably doing that anymore.

I still show up, and I try to look like I’m managing, but I’m not keeping up with the basic executive decisions the way I used to. Things sit on my desk, or in my inbox, or I keep rereading the same material and not moving it forward. Senior staff have started quietly taking over parts of my work—things I would never have handed off before. They don’t always say it directly, but I can tell. Meetings get redirected around me, someone else summarizes, someone else follows up, someone else makes sure the decision actually happens.

And at home it’s similar, maybe worse because I can’t hide it as well. My husband has had to take on most of the household responsibilities. I’ll say I’m going to do something and then I either don’t start it at all or I start and leave it half done. It’s embarrassing to say, because I’m used to being competent, but yes, my ability to work has dropped a lot.
Since this started, have you found yourself talking much less than usual or feeling emotionally flat compared with how you normally are?

Yes… yes, I have. That’s actually one of the things that scares me, because it’s not how I used to be at all.

I used to be very verbal, probably too verbal. At work I was the one driving the discussion, pushing ideas forward, calling people after openings or meetings, following up immediately, getting energy from it. I could talk through a problem for an hour and feel more alive afterward. Now I can sit at my desk for hours just staring at an agenda, knowing I’m supposed to say something or move the room toward a decision, and I just… don’t. It’s like the words are there somewhere, but I can’t make myself care enough to pull them out.

And at home, too. My husband will ask me normal things, simple things, and I’ll answer with a few words or not really answer at all. It isn’t that I’m angry at him. I’m not trying to punish anyone. I just feel sort of emptied out. Flat. Like everything has the same weight, or no weight.

The strange part is that it includes things I used to love about my work. I used to feel proud or excited or stressed in a good way, like it mattered. Now sometimes I look at something that would have completely engaged me before, and I feel almost nothing. Just blank. So yes, I’m talking less, and I feel much less emotionally connected than I normally would.
At any point since this began, have the voices been present continuously for at least one full month?

Yes. I mean, yes, definitely longer than a month.

The voices—the ones that seem like they’re coming from the walls sometimes, or from my phone even when nothing is actually playing—those have been happening for about three months now. It’s not like it was just one bad week and then it stopped. I wish it had been that. It’s been this ongoing thing, and even when I try to tell myself it’s stress or I’m mishearing something, it keeps happening.

So yes, there has been at least a full month where they were still present. More like the past three months, on and off but continuing through that whole period.
From the very first time these experiences began, has it been at least six months?

Yes. It’s been more than six months. A lot more, really.

If I go back to the very beginning—not just when it became impossible to ignore, but when I first started feeling like something was… off—it started around the company expansion, when they put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division. That was about two years and four months ago.

At the time I kept telling myself it was just the pressure of the new role, because there was so much to build and so many people watching me. But if you’re asking from the first time these experiences began, then yes, it’s been well over six months. Around two years and four months.
